question.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -6 & 1 \\ 10 & -6 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $B$ in the mean-deviation form above, where the individual observations are given in columns. 
Find the sample covariance matrix of the data.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{4-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -6 & 1 \\ 10 & -6 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 10 \\ 5 & -6 \\ -6 & 5 \\ 1 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}62 & -69 \\ -69 & 242\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
